properties.name: Ragnarök — Twilight of the Gods
properties.summary: Ragnarök is the prophesied end of the Norse cosmos. Loki breaks free, the Midgard Serpent rises from the sea, Fenrir devours Odin, and Thor and the serpent kill each other. The world sinks into the sea, only to rise again green and renewed. Two human survivors repopulate the earth.

properties.name: Sigurd and Fafnir
properties.summary: The hero Sigurd, guided by the smith Regin, slew the dragon Fafnir and bathed in its blood, gaining near-invulnerability. He tasted the dragon's heart and could understand bird speech. He woke the Valkyrie Brynhild from her enchanted sleep. His story ends in betrayal and tragedy at the Burgundian court.

properties.name: Norse Creation — Ginnungagap
properties.summary: In the beginning was Ginnungagap, the yawning void between fire (Muspelheim) and ice (Niflheim). The frost giant Ymir formed from melting ice, nourished by the cosmic cow Audhumla. Odin and his brothers slew Ymir and fashioned the world from his body: his flesh became earth, blood became seas, skull became sky.

properties.name: Thor vs Jörmungandr
properties.summary: Thor and the Midgard Serpent Jörmungandr are fated enemies. Thor once nearly caught the serpent while fishing with the giant Hymir, using an ox head as bait. At Ragnarök, they will fight to their mutual destruction — Thor slays the serpent but falls dead from its venom after nine steps.

properties.name: Loki's Mischief and Punishment
properties.summary: Loki, the trickster god, caused endless trouble — cutting Thor's wife's hair, tricking blind Höðr into killing the beloved Balder, and scheming against the gods. Finally bound with serpent venom dripping on his face, he will break free at Ragnarök to lead the forces of chaos.

properties.name: Death of Balder
properties.summary: Balder, the most beloved god, had prophetic nightmares of death. Frigg extracted oaths from all things not to harm him — except mistletoe. Loki fashioned a mistletoe dart and guided blind Höðr to throw it, killing Balder. The gods tried to ransom him from Hel but Loki refused to weep, sealing Balder's death.

properties.name: Theft of the Mead of Poetry
properties.summary: The Mead of Poetry was brewed from the blood of the wisest being, Kvasir. Odin infiltrated the giant Suttung's mountain by seducing his daughter Gunnlöð. He drank all three cauldrons of mead and escaped as an eagle, spitting the mead into vessels in Asgard. Some spilled to earth, giving mortals poetry.

properties.name: Freyja and the Brísingamen
properties.summary: Freyja desired the Brísingamen, a necklace of incomparable beauty forged by four dwarves. She spent a night with each dwarf to obtain it. Loki stole it on Odin's orders, transforming into a flea to unpin the clasp. Heimdall fought Loki to recover it. The necklace became Freyja's most treasured possession.

properties.name: Valhalla — Hall of the Slain
properties.summary: Warriors who died bravely in battle were chosen by the Valkyries to feast in Odin's great hall Valhalla. Each day they fought to the death, each evening they were resurrected to feast on the boar Sæhrímnir and drink mead from the goat Heiðrún. They prepared for the final battle of Ragnarök.
